title: Pre-market stranded-value scan for legacy technical lineage
objective: Search for hidden resources whose value emerges under a specific state before a normal transaction exists.
truth_rules: PRE_MARKET STRANDED VALUE > IMPROVING AN EXISTING LISTING
MODEL-SPECIFIC TACIT KNOWLEDGE != GENERIC ENGINEERING LABOR

wide_scan.observed_pressure: One plant's obsolete spare inventory can be another plant's line-down critical part.
counterevidence: verified surplus/obsolete MRO catalogues already exist
enterprise surplus disposition platforms already identify and resell idle spares
reverse engineering and on-demand machining cover missing references
wide_scan.verdict: Exact-part-number surplus routing is already a developed specialty market.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: SMEs lack expensive testing/pilot equipment while public and enterprise equipment can be underused.
wide_scan.verdict: Government, industrial parks and specialist platforms are actively building the natural access/control plane.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: Factories face repetitive buyer due-diligence audits.
wide_scan.verdict: Sedex/SMETA already standardizes shareable audit evidence specifically to reduce duplicate audits.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: Legacy assets remain productive after OEM support, documentation and original human knowledge disappear; a line-down or migration can make former OEM/project-specific tacit knowledge disproportionately valuable.
actors: factory or asset owner with unsupported legacy equipment
legacy service integrator or maintenance contractor
former OEM / retired controls / commissioning / maintenance engineer
optional insurer, legal/forensic or engineering party

evidence.fact: A 2026 PLC migration case describes missing source, an engineer who retired a decade earlier and outdated printed logic.
A 2026 PLCtalk request explicitly seeks a retired Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controls engineer for paid consulting, preferring steel-industry experience.

A 2026 Motion case reports sourcing specialized obsolete-spindle repair partners including former employees of original manufacturers; reported repair turnaround was 3-4 weeks versus more than 20 weeks for replacement/reverse-engineered new spindles.
evidence.evidence_role: vendor case study; performance not independently audited

evidence.fact: Compass Engineering markets legacy instrument support from former OEM staff and factory-trained engineers.
A retired-engineer matching event connected veteran Japanese manufacturing engineers with industrial companies seeking technical guidance.
A technical-advisor search case reports identifying retiring/retired engineers using public patent and academic-paper traces for an industrial client.

counterevidence.fact: Specialist legacy controls firms already perform unsupported PLC/DCS migration, reverse engineering and logic recovery.
Generic expert networks already assemble engineering and former-executive specialists.
Reverse engineering can often substitute for unavailable original human knowledge.

wide_scan.structural_hypothesis: Technical-lineage matching by OEM/model/project/controls history may identify uniquely relevant former personnel who can reduce diagnostic uncertainty faster than generic service search.
not_yet_evidenced: frequency at which former-OEM/project-specific knowledge is decisive
safe/legal boundary for former employee knowledge
incremental value beyond specialist legacy-service firms
wide_scan.next_test: Run causal descent on when historical human lineage outperforms normal service, reverse engineering and generic expert search.

cross_scan_verdict.meta_learning: Tacit historical knowledge can be a stranded asset whose value is activated by a specific legacy-system failure state; the relevant routing key may be technical lineage rather than job title.

requirements: separate public professional history from proprietary employer knowledge
define safe advisory scope and liability
no recruitment, outreach, pricing or marketplace build
